html:
A peace treaty signed in 532 between Justinian's empire and Sasanian Persia under Khosrow I, ending the Iberian War of 527 to 531. It had no end date, hence its name.

The Romans paid 11,000 pounds of gold, presented as a contribution to the defence of the Caucasus passes against steppe raiders. Each side gave back forts it had taken. One clause let the pagan philosophers who had left Athens for Persia go home safely.

Justinian bought peace in the east so he could turn west: the next year Belisarius sailed for Africa in the Vandalic War. The peace held only eight years. In 540 Khosrow invaded Syria and sacked Antioch, and war went on, with truces, for another two decades.
sum: A peace treaty signed in 532 between Justinian's empire and Sasanian Persia under Khosrow I, ending the Iberian War of 527 to 531. It had no end date, hence its name.
